verdicts.note: Sitting judge (appointed September 2025 [S4]) with three-plus years as a Superior Court commissioner before that [S1][S4], running explicitly on 'Judicial experience matters' [S1]. About a year on the bench is short tenure, so -1 rather than -2. High confidence rests on the documented record.

Only formation and diversion evidence is used, as the judges' rule requires. Formation is mixed: solo civil practice for both plaintiffs and defendants, municipal prosecution in Battle Ground [S1][S4], and co-creating Battle Ground's first therapeutic court [S2]. The prosecution and diversion pieces roughly offset and the civil practice is uninformative. No bail position. 0 medium stands. The endorsements were correctly not used.

No judicial service [S1][S2], challenging a recently appointed sitting judge. He runs on courtroom and appellate experience (450+ felony cases, 50+ trials, about 20 appellate briefs [S1][S2]), not on newness, so +1 rather than +2.

Explicit interpretive statements: 'The role of a judge is to follow the law, not make it' and 'apply the law as written' [S2]. Considered +/-2: he states no originalism or textualism beyond that and adds 'respect the constitution', so -1 matches other as-written candidates in this election (e.g. Pierce and Supreme Court candidates scored -1 on similar language). Medium fits one source.

Direction is right: his formation is entirely criminal prosecution [S1], with drug-enforcement (Street Crimes Unit) and Crime Reduction Team assignments [S1][S2] and a pledge to hold 'people accountable' [S1]. But -2 overstates it. Judges' safety rests only on bail, diversion or formation evidence, and the dossier has no bail or sentencing position from him; he frames his career as 'the rule of law protects both public safety and individual rights' [S1]. Prosecution-only formations without bail positions are scored -1 elsewhere in this election (Renee Walls, 26 years; Bianca Tse, 16 years; Sven Nelson, about 30 years). Lervold's career is shorter than any of those. -1 medium keeps him consistent.
